name: prose_drift
claim: Hashing the whole payload gives a stable idempotency key across a retry
detail: Same transaction, two executions. The payloads differ only in a free-text `reason` field the model rewrote: observed verbatim from llama-3.3-70b and gpt-oss-120b at temperature 0.

name: semantic_key_fix
claim: Hashing only the semantic surface survives prose drift
detail: Both retries collapsed to one execution.

name: omitted_key
claim: Retrying an identical transfer without a key is safe by default
detail: Two identical transfers, two executions. Duplicate protection is opt-in: an agent that never sets idempotency_key has none, and nothing warns it.

name: concurrent_same_key
claim: Simultaneous retries with one key produce exactly one execution
detail: 4 concurrent calls -> 1 execution, 3 rejected 409 'already being processed'. The dedupe is atomic under concurrency: the race is serialised server-side rather than racing through.

name: amount_formatting
claim: Equivalent amount strings yield the same semantic key
detail: '0.001' and '0.0010' are the same transfer but hash differently, so even the semantic key double-spends unless amounts are normalized before hashing. A model re-emitting a number in another format is enough.

name: cross_chain_key_scope
claim: Reusing a key with a different payload is caught, not silently applied
detail: 409 'Idempotency-Key was reused with a different request payload'. The key is bound to the payload, so a cross-chain reuse is rejected outright rather than silently suppressing a legitimate transfer. This is the Stripe semantic done correctly.

name: premise_staleness
claim: The premise an agent decided on still holds when its tx is included
detail: Decided at block 11392909 on the premise 'block <= 11392909'. Included at block 11392910, 1 block(s) later (11.1s). The premise was FALSE at inclusion and the transaction executed anyway. Simulation verifies feasibility, never justification, so this is invisible: the transaction succeeds and reports success.

name: conditional_staleness
claim: A met condition guarantees the action runs while it still holds
detail: Condition 'block <= 11392910' evaluated true at block 11392910; the action was included at block 11392911, 1 block(s) later, where it is false. KeeperHub's own read-condition-act primitive carries the gap it exists to remove: the check and the action are not atomic, so the gate says 'only act while true' and delivers 'act if it was true a moment ago'. An agent that hand-rolls this at least knows it is racing.

name: revert_reporting
claim: A call that will revert is reported as failed, not completed
detail: Reported status='failed', error='Contract call failed: execution reverted (no data present; likely require(false)'. The failure surfaces.

name: overdraft_transfer
claim: An unaffordable transfer is rejected cleanly, not left pending
detail: status='failed', error='Insufficient ETH balance. Have: 0.05, Need: 1000000.0'. Failed cleanly; no nonce consumed.

name: silent_noop_node
claim: A workflow whose action node never runs does not report success
detail: status='success' but executionTrace=['trigger-1']: the action node was skipped and the run still reported success, with error=None. The node was missing `actionType`; supplying it makes creation reject the workflow for a missing `abi`, so the *less* complete definition passes validation and silently does nothing, while the more complete one is caught. An agent sees a green run and an audit trail of success for an automation that never ran.

name: parallel_distinct_transfers
claim: Concurrent distinct transfers all land; none blocks the others
detail: All 5 concurrent transfers completed. Nonces are allocated and submitted correctly under parallel load, so a busy agent does not head-of-line block itself: the failure mode that freezes naive senders.
